stimulus.title: Height of a Ferris wheel seat
stimulus.html: A Ferris wheel has a diameter of 40 meters, and its center is 25 meters above the ground. The wheel turns counterclockwise at a constant speed and completes one full turn every 8 minutes. At time t=0t = 0 minutes, seat SS is at the lowest point of the wheel. The sinusoidal function hh models the height of seat SS above the ground, in meters, at time tt. The graph of hh for one full turn is shown with its axes unscaled. The points FF, GG, JJ, KK and MM are on the graph: FF, JJ and MM are a lowest or highest point, and GG and KK are at the height of the center of the wheel.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Find the coordinates of the points FF, GG, JJ, KK and MM.

rubric.point: The extremes: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F = (0, 5)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>45</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J = (4, 45)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M = (8, 5)</annotation></semantics></math>

The midline points: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>25</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G = (2, 25)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>25</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K = (6, 25)</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: The radius is 20 m, so the seat's height goes from <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>25</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">25 - 20 = 5</annotation></semantics></math> m to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>25</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>45</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">25 + 20 = 45</annotation></semantics></math> m. A quarter turn takes <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>8</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{8}{4} = 2</annotation></semantics></math> minutes. <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F = (0, 5)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>25</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G = (2, 25)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>45</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J = (4, 45)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>25</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K = (6, 25)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M = (8, 5)</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: The function hh is given by h(t)h(t)=asin⁡(b(t+c))+d= a\sin(b(t + c)) + d, where aa, bb, cc and dd are constants. Find values of aa, bb, cc and dd.

accept: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b = -\frac{\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math> with a matching <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math>

rubric.point: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> that fit the graph: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a = 20</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c = -2</annotation></semantics></math>, or <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a = -20</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c = 2</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: any <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> that differs from these by a multiple of 8

a check that <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(0) = 5</annotation></semantics></math> with the chosen values

parts.sample: Midline <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>45</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d = \frac{45 + 5}{2} = 25</annotation></semantics></math>; amplitude <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>45</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{45 - 5}{2} = 20</annotation></semantics></math>; period 8, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>8</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b = \frac{2\pi}{8} = \frac{\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>. With <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a = 20</annotation></semantics></math>, the sine pattern starts (midline, rising) at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>G</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t + c = 0</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c = -2</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(t)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>20</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 20\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{4}(t - 2)\right) + 25</annotation></semantics></math>. Check: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(0)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>20</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 20\sin\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}\right) + 25</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 5</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: C(i)
parts.prompt: Is hh increasing or decreasing on the interval (2,4)(2, 4)? Give a reason for your answer in the context of the problem.

rubric.point: Increasing, with a reason: on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2, 4)</annotation></semantics></math> the seat moves from the height of the center (<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>G</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G</annotation></semantics></math>) up to the top of the wheel (<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J</annotation></semantics></math>)
accept: the seat is rising from 25 m to 45 m

parts.sample: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> is increasing on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2, 4)</annotation></semantics></math>: between <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 4</annotation></semantics></math> the seat rises from the height of the center, 25 m, to the top of the wheel, 45 m.

parts.label: C(ii)
parts.prompt: Is the rate of change of hh increasing or decreasing on the interval (2,4)(2, 4)? Explain your reasoning.

rubric.point: Decreasing, with a reason: the graph of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> is concave down on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2, 4)</annotation></semantics></math> (above the midline, bending toward the highest point <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J</annotation></semantics></math>), so the seat rises more and more slowly
accept: the rate of change of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> is decreasing because the graph is concave down

the average rates of change over equal pieces of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2, 4)</annotation></semantics></math> get smaller

parts.sample: The rate of change of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> is decreasing on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2, 4)</annotation></semantics></math>. The graph of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> is above its midline there and concave down: the seat is still rising, but more slowly as it nears the top, where its height stops changing.
